summary.text: Kim Ward is a Republican who has represented Pennsylvania's 39th Senatorial District since winning the seat in 2008 and serves as Senate President Pro Tempore for the 2023-2024 and 2025-2026 sessions; she was the first woman to hold that office.

paragraphs.text: Ward grew up in Meadowlands, Washington County, attended the Community College of Allegheny County respiratory therapy program, the University of Pittsburgh and Middle Tennessee State University, and worked as a board-certified respiratory therapist before entering government.
She served as a Westmoreland County Commissioner and chairwoman of the Hempfield Township Board of Supervisors.

Ward won the 39th District seat in 2008 and was re-elected in 2012, 2016, 2020 and 2024. She was Majority Caucus Administrator in 2019-2020 and Senate Majority Leader for 2021-2022, and her biography describes her as the first woman to serve as President Pro Tempore and Majority Leader.

As a breast cancer survivor, she sponsored legislation, signed as Act 1 of 2023, eliminating costs for breast MRIs, breast ultrasounds and BRCA-related genetic testing and counseling for high-risk Pennsylvanians insured under state law.
She and her husband, Dr. Thomas Ward, have three sons.
